title: The Gathas
author: zoroaster
attributionNote: Traditionally attributed to Zarathushtra. The date, authorship and interpretation of the Gathas are debated; the Avestan text is difficult and translations differ substantially.
description: The Gathas are the oldest hymns of the Avesta, attributed to Zarathushtra and embedded in the Yasna liturgy. They are central to Zoroastrian theology and ritual.
historicalContext: The Gathas were transmitted orally for centuries before being written down. Their archaic Avestan language and complex poetic form make translation and interpretation unusually contested.
availabilityNote: The Gathas are not a separate book in the Avesta: they are the seventeen hymns at the centre of the Yasna liturgy (Yasna XXVIII–LIII), and they are read there. This record is the catalogue entry for the hymns themselves; the complete text, in Mills's translation, is in the Avesta — Yasna work.
